I use iPhone Mirroring every single day to control my iPhone directly from my Mac, and the feature is getting even better this year. The public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate launch this month, bringing three major updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's everything you need to know about the new features.

macOS 27: iPhone Mirroring New Features

The biggest change coming to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window for any app that supports iOS 27. However, this currently only works with Apple's own iPhone apps. That said, once developers roll out iOS 27 updates later this year, support for resizing will expand rapidly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only offered three preset sizes: Smaller, Actual Size, and Larger. Changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27

expected to launch later this year.

macOS 27 and iOS 27 also bring several more iPhone Mirroring updates:

  • Control Center Access
  • DRM Video Support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring had no access to Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can launch Control Center using the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut, or via the Show menu in your Mac's menu bar.

DRM video support means that you can now watch copyright-protected video content through iPhone Mirroring on your Mac. Previously, when you launched iPhone Mirroring, any DRM-protected videos would just display a black screen.

macOS 27 also gives iPhone Mirroring a new app icon, which differs from many other built-in Apple app icons.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried the public betas yet? Drop your thoughts in the comments section below.
